audits.claim: Cache deletion leaves the connected-calendar status stale when no onSuccess callback is supplied and remains available when connection changes are disabled.
audits.evidence: packages/features/eventtypes/components/tabs/advanced/EventAdvancedTab.tsx:372-384 mounts the wrapper with disableConnectionModification=true and no onChanged; packages/platform/atoms/selected-calendars/wrappers/SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper.tsx:152-160,179-185 reads connectedCalendars without focus refetch and passes the absent callback through. packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:42-50 only shows a toast and invokes the optional callback, whereas packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts:28-30 actually removes the rows. With an existing Google cache, delete it in this view: the existing cacheUpdatedAt prop and menu remain stale because this mutation never invalidates the query (unlike disconnect at lines 61-63); the shared client configuration at packages/trpc/react/trpc.ts:100-123 has no automatic mutation invalidation. Lines 67-69 also confirm that disabling connection modification hides disconnect but does not hide cache deletion, although whether that latter distinction is undesirable is a product-policy question.

audits.claim: The connectedCalendars handler bypasses the feature-gated cache factory and performs its status query even when calendar caching is disabled.
audits.evidence: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts:27-29 constructs CalendarCacheRepository directly and always awaits its status method. packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.ts:22-28 instead checks the global calendar-cache flag and returns the mock when disabled; packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts:27-29 would return an empty list. The concrete repository runs groupBy at packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-182, so the unnecessary disabled-feature database read is confirmed. This is a feature-gating/performance consistency concern; no measured slowdown or failing availability path is established.

audits.claim: The migration warning contradicts its default, and pre-existing cache rows receive migration-time freshness timestamps.
audits.evidence: packages/prisma/migrations/20250715160635_add_calendar_cache_updated_at/migration.sql:4 says there is no default, but line 9 explicitly adds NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so existing rows are initialized to migration time. packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:173-186 takes the maximum updatedAt, which packages/features/apps/components/CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx:88-95 presents as Last updated. An existing row cached before deployment will therefore display deployment time until refreshed; the 30-day cache lifetime is defined at packages/features/calendar-cache/calendar-cache.repository.ts:14-16. This confirms a stale comment and a temporary metadata inaccuracy, without changing the cached availability or its expiration.

audits.claim: Removing satisfies from SelectedCalendarRepository.findMany removes Prisma argument type checking.
audits.evidence: packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts:259-260 now passes the object directly to prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany, whose typed parameter still checks the supplied where, select and orderBy. The wrapper also retains its explicit FindManyArgs type at lines 13-35, including Prisma.SelectedCalendarSelect. The diff removes an intermediate satisfies expression, not the typed Prisma call, so the alleged loss of the type guard does not follow.
